2. Arjuna Award (Second highest Sporting honour)

  • Instituted: 1961
  • ₹15 Lakh given to recipients.
  • First Recipients (1961):
  • P.G. Sethi - Golf
  • Bajarangi Prasad - Swimming
  • Karni Singh - Shooting
  • Krishna Das - Archery
  • Udey Chand - Wrestling
  • P.K. Banerjee - Football
  • Kumari Ann Lumsden - Hockey
  • Salim Durrani - Cricket
  • Gurbachan Singh Randhawa - Athletics
  • 1st Woman to get Arjuna Award: Meena Shah (1962) for Badminton.
  • 1st Arjuna Award recipient for Kabaddi: Sahanand Mahadev Shetty (1972).

3. Dronacharya Award

  • Given to coaches for producing outstanding sportspersons at the international level.
  • Instituted: 1985
  • First Recipients (1985): Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat (Wrestling), O.M. Nambiar (Athletics), Om Prakash Bhardwaj (Boxing).
  • First female recipient: Hansa Sharma (Wrestling) in 2000.

#### Dronacharya Awardees for 2024:

CategorySportsNames
Regular CategoryPara-ShootingSubhash Rana
HockeySandeep Sangwan
Lifetime CategoryBadmintonS Muralidharan

4. Dhyan Chand Award (or Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement Award in Sports & Games)

  • Given to retired sportspersons for their lifetime contribution to sports.
  • Instituted: 2002
  • First Recipients: Shahuraj Birajdar (Boxing), Ashok Diwan (Hockey), Aparna Ghosh (Basketball).

LITERARY AWARDS

1. Jnanpith Award (Highest Literary Award)

  • Given to writers for their literary excellence in any of the 22 languages of India as listed in 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India.
  • Given by: The Bhartiya Jnanpith.
  • Prize amount of Rs. 11 lakhs, a citation and a bronze replica of Goddess Saraswati is awarded.
  • Instituted in: 1961
  • First Recipient (1965): G. Sankara Kurup for Odakkuzhal (Malayalam) which means The Bamboo Flute, published in 1950.
  • First female Recipient (1976): Ashapoorna Devi for her novel Pratham Pratishruti.
  • 58th Jnanpith Awardee (2024): Vinod Kumar Shukla and Jagadguru Rambhadracharya.
  • Damodar Mauzo (Konkani writer) won the 57th Jnanpith Award.

2. Sahitya Akademi Award

  • Given to writers for their literary excellence in one of the 24 recognised Indian languages including English and Hindi.
  • Instituted: 1954
  • First Recipient in Hindi Category, 1955: Makhan Lal Chaturvedi for Him-Tarangini (poetry).
  • First Recipient in English Category, 1960: R.K. Narayan for his novel The Guide.

3. Saraswati Samman

  • Annual award for outstanding literary works published in any of India's 22 official languages, listed in 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India.
  • Instituted: 1991
  • Given by: K.K. Birla Foundation
  • First Recipient: Harivansh Rai Bachchan (Hindi) - 1991

4. Vyas Samman

  • Annual award given for outstanding literary works in Hindi.
  • Instituted: 1991
  • Given by: K.K. Birla Foundation
  • First Recipient: 1991 - Ram Vilas Sharma for his book Bharat ke Pracheen Bhasha Parivar aur Hindi

FILMS AND ENTERTAINMENT AWARDS

1. Dadasaheb Phalke Award (Highest Film Honour)

  • For Lifetime contribution to Indian cinema.
  • First Recipient: Devika Rani (1969)
  • Dadasaheb Phalke Awardee for 2024: Mithun Chakraborty

GLOBAL AWARDS

1. Nobel Prize

  • Instituted: 1901 by the Nobel Foundation (Sweden/Norway)
  • 6 Categories: Peace, Literature, Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Economics.
  • All Nobel prize is awarded in Stockholm, Sweden while Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
  • First Recipient: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (Physics, 1901) - for the discovery of X-rays.
  • First female recipient: Marie Curie (1903) - Only women to win 2 Nobel:

— Shared 1st Nobel with her husband Pierre Curie & Henri Becquerel.

— Won 2nd Nobel in 1911 for the discovery of Radium & Polonium.

Nobel Prize for Economics was established in 1968 by Sweden's Central Bank. Originally known as Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences.

Nobel prize is given in the memory of Alfred Nobel (discoverer of Dynamite).

  • First Indian Recipient: Rabindranath Tagore (Literature) 1913 for Geetanjali.

Okay, smarty- if you are really that brilliant, then — Can you recall what is Raman effect?

Other Indian Recipients:

  • C.V. Raman - Physics, 1930
  • Mother Teresa - Peace, 1979
  • Amartya Sen - Economic Sciences, 1998
  • Venkatraman Ramakrishnan - Chemistry, 2009
  • Kailash Satyarthi - Peace (for struggle against child labour), 2014
  • Abhijit Banerjee - Economic Sciences (work in poverty alleviation), 2019

Abel Prize is considered as Nobel Prize of Maths.

2. Ramon Magsaysay Award

  • Named after Ramon Magsaysay, former President of Philippines (known for integrity and public service).
  • Instituted: 1957 by the Rockefeller Brothers Fund (Philippines).
  • First Recipient: Wu San Lien (Public Service, 1958).
  • First Indian Recipient: Acharya Vinoba Bhave, 1958.

Other Indian Recipients:

  • Kiran Bedi - Government Service, 1994
  • Aruna Roy - Community Leadership, 2000
  • Bezwaada Wilson - Emergent Leadership, 2016
  • Ravish Kumar - Ethical Journalism, 2019
  • Dr. Ravi Kannan - Public service in medical field, 2023

3. Booker Prize

  • Instituted: 1969 (UK)
  • For Best original novel written in English and published in the UK or Ireland.
  • First Recipient: P.H. Newby - Something to Answer For, 1969.
  • First Indian Recipient: Arundhati Roy - The God of Small Things, 1997.

Other Indian Recipients:

  • Kiran Desai - The Inheritance of Loss, 2006
  • Aravind Adiga - The White Tiger, 2008
  • Geetanjali Shree - Tomb of Sand (International Booker), 2022

Note: The International Booker Prize is awarded for a book translated into English and shared between the author and the translator.

4. Pulitzer Prize

  • Instituted: 1917 by the will of Joseph Pulitzer (USA).
  • Awarded by: Columbia University, New York.
  • Categories: Journalism, Literature, Drama, Music, etc.
  • First Recipient: Herbert Bayard Swope (Reporting, 1917).
  • First Indian Recipient: Gobind Behari Lal - Journalism (Science Reporting), 1937.

Other Indian Recipients:

  • → Jhumpa Lahiri - Interpreter of Maladies (Fiction), 2000.
  • → Geeta Anand - Wall Street Journal investigative reporting, 2003.
  • → Siddhartha Mukherjee - The Emperor of All Maladies (General Nonfiction), 2011.
  • → Indian Staff of Reuters - Photography, 2020 (for coverage of protests in Hong Kong).

5. OSCAR Awards (Also known as The Academy Awards)

  • Instituted in: 1929
  • First Recipient: Emil Jannings (Best Actor) & Janet Gaynor (Best Actress).
  • First Indian Recipient: Bhanu Athaiya (Best Costume Design, Gandhi - 1983).
  • Satyajit Ray is the first Indian to receive an Honorary Oscar (1992).
  • A. R. Rahman is the first Indian to win two Oscars in the same year (2009).
  • The Elephant Whisperers (2023) was India's first win in the Documentary Short Film Category.

#### Oscar Awards 2025 Winners:

  • Best Picture: Anora
  • Best Director: Sean Baker (Anora)
  • Best Actor: Adrien Brody (The Brutalist)
  • Best Actress: Mikey Madison (Anora)
  • Best Supporting Actor: Kieran Culkin (A Real Pain)
  • Best Supporting Actress: Zoe Saldana (Emilia Pérez)
  • Best Animated Feature: Flow
  • Best International Feature Film: I'm Still Here
  • Best Original Screenplay: Anora
  • Best Adapted Screenplay: Conclave

Emmy awards are given in Television Industry and Grammy Awards are given in Music Industry.

Key concepts

  • Bharat Ratna (Highest Civilian Award)
  • Padma Awards (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri)
  • Gallantry Awards (Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra)
  • Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna & Arjuna Award
  • Jnanpith Award (Highest Literary)
  • Nobel Prize (Indian Recipients: Tagore, C.V. Raman, Amartya Sen, Abhijit Banerjee)
  • Dadasaheb Phalke Award (Film)
  • Booker Prize / Pulitzer Prize / Oscar (Indian Connections)
